sections.h2: Who to call about a tax question
sections.html:
Three county offices share 41 South Central Avenue in Clayton. The Assessor values real estate and personal property. The Board of Equalization hears disputes over that value. The Collector of Revenue, part of the Department of Revenue, sends the bills and takes the payments.

St. Louis County tax offices in Clayton
OfficePhoneEmailHours
Assessor, 3rd floor314-615-2555Assessor@stlouiscountymo.govCounter Mon to Thu 8:00 to 3:30; phone Mon to Fri 8:30 to 4:30
Board of Equalization314-615-7195boe@stlouiscountymo.govSame schedule as the Assessor
Collector of Revenue314-615-7100collector@stlouiscountymo.govCounter Mon to Thu 8:00 to 3:30

The Collector bills for more than 200 taxing districts, so two homes in the same city can receive very different totals. Go through the district list on your bill line by line, because each line is a separate taxing body.

St. Louis County is Missouri's most populous, with 1,004,125 residents counted in 2020 and an estimate of 990,911 for July 1, 2025, down 1.4% from the 2020 base. It has 448,637 housing units and 413,849 households. Owners live in about 69.2% of them, a typical owned home is valued at $276,800, typical rent is $1,209 and typical household income is $82,936. Commutes average 23.1 minutes.

Dozens of municipalities and 23 public school districts, including Rockwood, Parkway, Lindbergh, Mehlville, Pattonville, Ritenour and Ferguson-Florissant, sit inside the county. The school line on a tax bill varies widely from one address to the next.

State law requires the County Assessor to reassess all real estate in the county every odd-numbered year. The next reassessment is 2027.

When a notice arrives, compare the value and the property class with what you know about the house. Then decide whether to call the Assessor at 314-615-2555 before the appeal window closes. The Assessor answers value questions by phone on weekdays, while in-person visits run Monday through Thursday.

You appeal to the Board of Equalization, which is separate from the Assessor. The board hears value disputes for homeowners, businesses and manufacturers and also considers exemption requests from not-for-profit organizations. Contact it at 314-615-7195 or boe@stlouiscountymo.gov.

  • Deadline: RSMo 137.275 requires the appeal to be lodged with the board on or before the second Monday in July. The next is July 12, 2027.
  • Method: you may appeal in person, through an attorney or agent, or in writing.
  • Burden of proof: RSMo 138.060 says there is no presumption that the assessor's valuation is correct, and in a charter county with more than one million inhabitants the assessor must prove the value does not exceed true market value. Ask the board how that rule applies to your case.
  • Next step: the State Tax Commission hears appeals from the board's decision. Ask the board for its current filing instructions.

To support a lower number, bring a recent appraisal, a purchase contract, comparable sales or repair estimates.

Penalties begin after January 1. RSMo 139.100 directs the Collector to collect a penalty on unpaid tax after the first day of January, using the amount in RSMo 140.100, which is 18% of each year's delinquency for land in the back tax book. For land redeemed before a sale, the penalty cannot exceed 2% per month or fraction of a month.

Mailing counts. The same statute treats a payment delivered by United States mail as paid on the postmark date, and certified or registered mail uses the registration date. If the postmark falls within the allowed period, no added tax or penalty applies. The Collector's page links to a Pay Taxes page, a tax rates lookup and a customer service portal at csportal.stlouiscountymo.gov.

If your bill looks wrong, call 314-615-7100 before you pay, and keep any corrected statement with your closing papers.

The county tax bill is part of every closing here. Title companies ask for a payoff or proration for the current year, and an unpaid prior year carries the 18% penalty described above. Ask the Collector for the balance on your parcel, then give the figure to the closing agent.

If a lender pays your tax from escrow, confirm that the last bill was paid before you list. If a senior tax freeze is on your account, ask the Collector how it is treated when the property changes hands.

The Collector also handles the county's tax sale for delinquent parcels. The counter is closed on Fridays and weekends, so a seller who needs a same-week payoff letter should phone early in the week or pay by mail or online. Owners who are behind should ask the Collector for payoff figures and sale dates at 314-615-7100 instead of waiting for a notice.

An overdue balance is paid from your sale proceeds, so it does not stop a sale. It can, however, slow one down if no one has asked for the payoff early. A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender, which helps when you have a deadline. Compare any offer with what a regular listing would net after commission and repairs, and make sure the settlement statement shows the tax line cleared.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
1. Find your parcel's current value and property class on the Assessor's notice, and call 314-615-2555 if either looks off.
  2. Check the district lines on your latest bill so you can tell buyers which schools and services the address carries.
  3. Ask the Collector for the balance on the parcel, including any older year, and pay what is overdue so the 18% penalty stops growing.
  4. If your lender escrows the tax, confirm the last bill was paid.
  5. Gather evidence if you plan to appeal: an appraisal, a purchase contract, comparable sales or repair estimates.
  6. Give the closing agent the payoff figure and keep the stamped envelope or receipt for any mailed payment.

The offices in Clayton keep short counter hours, Monday through Thursday, so plan any in-person errand for early in the week. Phone and email reach most of these offices without a trip downtown.

faqs.a: Third floor of 41 South Central Avenue, Clayton, MO 63105. Phones are staffed 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays, and the counter is open Monday through Thursday, 8:00 to 3:30.
The Board of Equalization, reached at 314-615-7195 or boe@stlouiscountymo.gov. It operates apart from the Assessor and takes appeals from homeowners, businesses and manufacturers.

faqs.q: What is the filing cutoff for an appeal?
faqs.a: Missouri statute fixes it at the second Monday of July, which is July 12 in 2027. Owners may appear personally, send an agent or attorney, or write.

faqs.q: Do all St. Louis County owners pay the same rate?
faqs.a: No. More than 200 taxing districts appear in the Collector's system, and the ones that cover your parcel set what you owe. A house in one school district can pay differently from a similar house in the next.

faqs.q: Does a postmark on the last day count?
faqs.a: Yes, if it travels by U.S. mail. RSMo 139.100 treats the postmark date as the payment date, and certified or registered mail uses the date of registration. Keep the stamped envelope or receipt.
